name: Prometheus Steals Fire
summary: Prometheus, a Titan, stole fire from Mount Olympus and gave it to humanity, enabling civilization. Zeus punished him by chaining him to a rock where an eagle ate his liver daily, only for it to regenerate each night. Heracles eventually freed him. The myth symbolizes the price of knowledge and defiance of divine authority.
significance: Foundational myth about human progress, sacrifice for knowledge, and the tension between divine and human power.

name: The Odyssey
summary: After the Trojan War, Odysseus spent ten years trying to return home to Ithaca. He faced the Cyclops, Sirens, Scylla and Charybdis, and the enchantress Circe. Meanwhile, his wife Penelope fended off suitors. The epic explores nostos (homecoming), cunning over brute force, and the costs of hubris.
significance: One of Western literature's foundational texts, establishing the archetype of the hero's journey home.

name: Wrath of Achilles (Iliad)
summary: The Iliad focuses on a few weeks during the tenth year of the Trojan War. Achilles withdraws from battle after Agamemnon takes his war prize. When Patroclus is killed by Hector, Achilles returns in devastating fury, slaying Hector and dragging his body around Troy. The poem ends with Hector's funeral.
significance: The Iliad defined the concept of heroic honor (kleos) and tragic mortality that shaped Western literary tradition.

name: Twelve Labors of Heracles
summary: Driven mad by Hera, Heracles killed his family. As penance, he completed twelve impossible labors: slaying the Nemean Lion, killing the Lernaean Hydra, capturing the Ceryneian Hind, and more. The final labor required him to bring Cerberus from the underworld. These trials earned him immortality.
significance: The archetypal hero's journey of redemption through impossible tasks, copied across countless cultures and stories.

name: Orpheus and Eurydice
summary: The musician Orpheus descended to the underworld to retrieve his dead wife Eurydice. His music moved Hades, who agreed to release her if Orpheus did not look back. At the last moment, Orpheus glanced back, losing Eurydice forever. The myth explores the power and limits of art and love.
significance: Archetypal myth of love beyond death that inspired centuries of opera, poetry, and film.

dna.moralLesson: Knowledge can elevate humanity, but it always carries ethical responsibility and cost.

name: Greek Creation (Chaos to Olympians)
summary: From primordial Chaos emerged Gaia (Earth), Tartarus (Abyss), and Eros (Love). Gaia bore Uranus (Sky), whose children the Titans were imprisoned until Kronos castrated his father. Zeus then overthrew Kronos, establishing the Olympian order. This succession myth mirrors Near Eastern creation patterns.
significance: Established the concept of divine succession and cosmic evolution from chaos to order that pervades Western thought.

name: Persephone and the Seasons
summary: Hades abducted Persephone to the underworld. Her mother Demeter, goddess of harvest, caused the earth to become barren in grief. Zeus brokered a compromise: Persephone would spend part of the year below and part above. Her return brings spring; her descent brings winter.
significance: One of the earliest etiological myths explaining seasonal change, central to the Eleusinian Mysteries.

Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Greek Mythology ve Mesopotamian Mythology arasindaki benzerlik, metin aktarimi ve temas aglariyla aciklanabilir; motifler yerel baglamda yeniden bicimlenmistir.

name: Romulus and Remus
summary: Twin sons of Mars and the Vestal Virgin Rhea Silvia, abandoned on the Tiber and raised by a she-wolf. As adults they founded a city, but quarreled over its location. Romulus killed Remus and named the city Rome. The fratricide shadowed Roman history with themes of necessary violence.
significance: Foundation myth that defined Roman identity and justified the city's martial character and territorial expansion.

dna.moralLesson: Human flourishing requires aligning personal desire with communal and cosmic responsibility.

name: The Aeneid
summary: After Troy fell, the hero Aeneas journeyed to Italy guided by destiny. He loved and abandoned Queen Dido of Carthage, descended to the underworld, and fought wars in Latium. His descendants would found Rome. Virgil's epic connected Roman power to Trojan heritage and divine mandate.
significance: Rome's national epic, linking Roman civilization to divine destiny and providing ideological foundation for Augustus's empire.

name: Ragnarök — Twilight of the Gods
summary: Ragnarök is the prophesied end of the Norse cosmos. Loki breaks free, the Midgard Serpent rises from the sea, Fenrir devours Odin, and Thor and the serpent kill each other. The world sinks into the sea, only to rise again green and renewed. Two human survivors repopulate the earth.
significance: A uniquely Norse concept of cyclical destruction and renewal, where even gods face death — profoundly influencing modern fantasy.

name: Sigurd and Fafnir
summary: The hero Sigurd, guided by the smith Regin, slew the dragon Fafnir and bathed in its blood, gaining near-invulnerability. He tasted the dragon's heart and could understand bird speech. He woke the Valkyrie Brynhild from her enchanted sleep. His story ends in betrayal and tragedy at the Burgundian court.
significance: The supreme hero myth of Nordic literature, directly inspiring Wagner's Ring Cycle and Tolkien's works.

name: Norse Creation — Ginnungagap
summary: In the beginning was Ginnungagap, the yawning void between fire (Muspelheim) and ice (Niflheim). The frost giant Ymir formed from melting ice, nourished by the cosmic cow Audhumla. Odin and his brothers slew Ymir and fashioned the world from his body: his flesh became earth, blood became seas, skull became sky.
significance: A unique creation-through-sacrifice myth where the cosmos is literally built from a slain primordial being.

name: Epic of Gilgamesh
summary: King Gilgamesh of Uruk, two-thirds god, befriended the wild man Enkidu. Together they slew Humbaba and the Bull of Heaven. When Enkidu died, Gilgamesh sought immortality from flood-survivor Utnapishtim. He found the plant of youth but a serpent stole it. He returned home accepting mortality, his legacy being the walls of Uruk.
significance: The oldest known literary work in human history, establishing themes of friendship, mortality, and the meaning of civilization.

name: Enuma Elish — Babylonian Creation
summary: From the mixing of sweet water (Apsu) and salt water (Tiamat) came the first gods. When Apsu plotted to destroy them, Enki killed him. Tiamat raised an army of monsters. Marduk slew Tiamat, splitting her body to form heaven and earth. Humans were created from Kingu's blood to serve the gods.
significance: Mesopotamian creation epic that directly influenced Genesis and established the combat-creation myth pattern.

name: Ishtar's Descent to the Underworld
summary: Ishtar descended through the seven gates of the underworld, removing one garment at each gate until she stood naked before her sister Ereshkigal, queen of the dead. The world above withered without her. She was rescued but had to send a substitute — her lover Tammuz, who would spend half the year below.
significance: One of the earliest descent myths, establishing the dying-and-rising deity pattern that influenced later religions.

name: The Great Flood (Utnapishtim)
summary: The gods decided to destroy humanity with a flood. Enki warned Utnapishtim, who built a great boat and loaded it with animals and craftsmen. After seven days the flood subsided. Utnapishtim released a dove, swallow, and raven. The gods granted him immortality. This predates the biblical Noah story.
significance: The oldest written flood narrative, directly ancestral to the biblical deluge story and over 200 global flood myths.

name: Osiris, Isis, and Set
summary: Set murdered his brother Osiris, dismembering and scattering his body across Egypt. Isis gathered the pieces and resurrected Osiris long enough to conceive Horus. Osiris became lord of the dead. Horus grew up to challenge Set, eventually winning kingship. This myth established the pharaonic succession pattern.
significance: Central Egyptian myth establishing concepts of resurrection, divine kingship, and the afterlife that influenced Christianity.

name: Journey Through the Duat (Book of the Dead)
summary: Each night Ra traveled through the twelve hours of the Duat (underworld), battling the serpent Apophis. Dead souls followed the same path, facing trials and gates guarded by demons. In the Hall of Two Truths, Anubis weighed the heart against Ma'at's feather. Ammit devoured those who failed.
significance: The most elaborate afterlife mythology in the ancient world, influencing later religious concepts of judgment and paradise.

name: Creation by Atum at Heliopolis
summary: Atum emerged from the primordial waters of Nun atop the first mound (benben). Through self-creation, he produced Shu (air) and Tefnut (moisture). They bore Geb (earth) and Nut (sky), who were separated by their father Shu. This Ennead of nine gods formed the basis of Egyptian cosmology.
significance: One of several competing Egyptian creation accounts, establishing the primordial mound concept that inspired pyramid architecture.

name: Mahabharata — Kurukshetra War
summary: The great war between the Pandava and Kaurava cousins for the throne of Hastinapura lasted eighteen days. Krishna served as Arjuna's charioteer, delivering the Bhagavad Gita on the battlefield. The Pandavas won but at devastating cost, with almost all warriors dead. The epic addresses dharma, duty, and cosmic justice.
significance: The longest epic poem ever written, containing the Bhagavad Gita — one of the world's most influential philosophical texts.

name: Ramayana — Rama's Journey
summary: Prince Rama was exiled for fourteen years with his wife Sita and brother Lakshmana. The demon king Ravana abducted Sita to Lanka. Rama allied with Hanuman and the monkey army, built a bridge across the ocean, and defeated Ravana. He returned to Ayodhya as king, celebrated as the festival Diwali.
significance: One of Asia's most beloved epics, performed and retold across Southeast Asia, embodying ideals of honor, devotion, and righteous rule.

name: Churning of the Ocean of Milk
summary: Devas and Asuras cooperated to churn the cosmic ocean using Mount Mandara as a churning rod and Vasuki the serpent as a rope. From the ocean emerged treasures: Lakshmi, the divine physician, the moon, and the elixir of immortality (amrita). Vishnu as Mohini tricked the Asuras to ensure only the Devas drank the amrita.
significance: Epic myth explaining the origin of divine treasures and the eternal struggle between order and chaos in Hindu cosmology.

name: Pangu Creates the World
summary: Pangu was born inside a cosmic egg of chaos. He grew for 18,000 years, pushing heaven and earth apart. When he died, his body became the world: breath became wind, voice became thunder, eyes became sun and moon, blood became rivers, and parasites on his body became humanity.
significance: China's primary creation myth, establishing the concept of cosmic sacrifice that resonates across Asian mythology.

name: Nüwa Creates Humanity
summary: After Pangu created the world, the goddess Nüwa was lonely. She shaped humans from yellow clay — carefully crafting nobles by hand and flinging drops of mud for commoners. She also repaired the sky when it was torn, using five colored stones. With her brother-husband Fuxi, she established marriage and civilization.
significance: A uniquely feminine creation myth that explains both human origins and social hierarchy in Chinese thought.

name: Journey to the West — Monkey King
summary: Sun Wukong, born from a stone egg, achieved immortality and wreaked havoc in Heaven before being imprisoned under a mountain by Buddha for 500 years. Released to accompany the monk Xuanzang on a pilgrimage to India for Buddhist scriptures, he protected the monk through 81 trials with his magical abilities.
significance: One of the four great classical novels of Chinese literature, blending Buddhist, Taoist, and folk traditions into an enduring adventure.

name: Izanagi and Izanami Create Japan
summary: The divine couple Izanagi and Izanami stirred the cosmic ocean with a jeweled spear, and drops formed the Japanese islands. They created gods, but Izanami died giving birth to fire. Izanagi descended to Yomi (underworld) but fled in horror at her decayed form. Purifying himself, he birthed Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi, and Susanoo.
significance: Japan's foundational creation myth, establishing the divine lineage of the imperial family and the islands' sacred origin.

name: Amaterasu and the Cave
summary: Offended by her brother Susanoo's violence, Amaterasu hid in a cave, plunging the world into darkness. The gods gathered outside, and Amenouzume performed an ecstatic dance that made them laugh. Curious, Amaterasu peeked out and was pulled into the light. The world was illuminated again.
significance: Explains the origin of solar eclipses and the power of ritual performance, central to Shinto practice.

name: Dangun — Founding of Korea
summary: Hwanung, son of the Lord of Heaven, descended to Mount Baekdu. A bear and tiger wished to become human. Given garlic and mugwort in a cave for 100 days, only the bear persevered, becoming a woman. She married Hwanung and bore Dangun, who founded Gojoseon (Old Korea) in 2333 BCE.
significance: The foundational myth of Korean national identity, still celebrated on National Foundation Day (Gaecheonjeol).

name: Five Suns — Aztec Creation Cycles
summary: The Aztec cosmos underwent five creations (Suns), each destroyed by a different cataclysm. The first by jaguars, second by wind, third by fire-rain, fourth by flood. In the fifth (current) Sun, the humble god Nanahuatzin sacrificed himself by jumping into fire to become the sun, requiring blood sacrifice to maintain its movement.
significance: Aztec cosmology uniquely demanded blood sacrifice to sustain the current world age, driving much of their religious and political practice.

name: Popol Vuh — Hero Twins
summary: The Hero Twins, Hunahpu and Xbalanque, descended to the underworld Xibalba to avenge their father. Through cleverness they defeated the Lords of Death in ball games and trials. They were sacrificed, ground up, and thrown into a river, but regenerated. They tricked the lords into being sacrificed and rose as the sun and moon.
significance: The K'iche' Maya creation epic, one of the most important pre-Columbian texts, revealing complex theology and cosmology.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Maya ve Egyptian gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Tur farki: Hero ve Afterlife odaklari ayridir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Maya Mythology ile Egyptian Mythology arasindaki baglanti kayda degerdir ancak literaturde nedensel model konusunda net uzlasi yoktur.

name: Viracocha Creates the World
summary: Viracocha rose from Lake Titicaca and created the sun, moon, and stars. He fashioned humans from stone but was unsatisfied. He caused a great flood, then created humans again from clay, giving each nation its language, songs, and customs. He walked across the Pacific and vanished, promising to return.
significance: Foundation myth of the Inca Empire, establishing the sacred origin of Lake Titicaca and justifying Inca dominion through divine mandate.

parallels.connectionExplanation: Inca Mythology ile Mesopotamian Mythology arasindaki baglanti kayda degerdir ancak literaturde nedensel model konusunda net uzlasi yoktur.

name: Perun vs Veles
summary: The thunder god Perun eternally battles the chthonic serpent-god Veles, who steals cattle, water, or Perun's wife from the heavens. Perun hurls lightning to strike Veles, who hides in trees, animals, or water. The cycle of theft and retribution mirrors the seasonal cycle and the cosmic order.
significance: The central Slavic mythological conflict, preserving ancient Indo-European storm-god vs serpent patterns found from India to Scandinavia.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Slavic ve Norse gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Tur farki: Cosmology ve War odaklari ayridir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Slavic Mythology ile Norse Mythology arasindaki paralellik daha eski bir anlati havuzundan dallanma ihtimaline isaret eder; filolojik ve yapisal okumalar birlikte kullanilir.

dna.moralLesson: Order is never final; every generation must defend meaning against returning chaos.

name: Ergenekon — Birth of the Turks
summary: After a devastating defeat, the last surviving Turks fled to the mythical Ergenekon valley, surrounded by impassable mountains. For generations they lived in isolation. When they grew too numerous, a blacksmith melted the iron mountain with a great fire, and a grey wolf (Bozkurt) led them out to conquer the steppe.
significance: Central founding myth of Turkic peoples, symbolizing rebirth from near-extinction and the wolf-ancestor motif found across Turkic cultures.

name: Seven Labors of Rostam
summary: The greatest hero of Persian legend, Rostam, completed seven impossible tasks to rescue King Kavus: slaying a lion, surviving the desert, defeating a dragon, overcoming a sorceress, capturing a demon, surviving a storm, and slaying the White Demon. His tragic fate was killing his own son Sohrab in battle.
significance: The central heroic narrative of the Shahnameh, Iran's national epic, embodying Persian ideals of honor, loyalty, and tragic fate.

name: Maui Fishes Up Islands & Snares the Sun
summary: The demigod Maui was a supreme trickster. He fished up the North Island of New Zealand using his grandmother's jawbone as a hook. He snared the sun with ropes to slow its journey and give people more daylight. He stole fire from the underworld goddess Mahuika. He died attempting to win immortality by crawling through the goddess of death.
significance: Maui myths span all of Polynesia, representing one of the most widespread trickster cycles in world mythology.

name: The Rainbow Serpent
summary: In the Dreamtime, the Rainbow Serpent slithered across the flat land, creating rivers, valleys, and ridges with its massive body. It established the laws of behavior and consequence. Those who obey prosper; those who break the law are turned to stone. It still sleeps in waterways, maintaining the natural order.
significance: One of the world's oldest continuous religious narratives, central to Aboriginal Australian spirituality and land stewardship.

name: Creation of the World (Yoruba)
summary: Olodumare sent Obatala to create land by pouring sand from a snail shell onto the primordial ocean. A chicken scratched the sand to spread it, forming land. Obatala shaped humans from clay but got drunk on palm wine, creating those with disabilities. Oduduwa completed the task, founding Ile-Ife, the sacred city.
significance: Foundation myth of Yoruba civilization and the city of Ile-Ife, one of the most influential African creation narratives.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Yoruba ve Chinese gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Ayni turde olsalar da rituel islevleri ayrisir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Yoruba Mythology ile Chinese Mythology arasindaki baglanti kayda degerdir ancak literaturde nedensel model konusunda net uzlasi yoktur.

dna.moralLesson: Order is never final; every generation must defend meaning against returning chaos.

name: Forging of the Sampo
summary: The eternal sage Väinämöinen commissioned the smith Ilmarinen to forge the Sampo, a magical artifact that produced flour, salt, and gold. It was given to Louhi, mistress of Pohjola (the North), as a bride-price. When Väinämöinen, Ilmarinen, and Lemminkäinen attempted to steal it back, the Sampo was shattered in a sea battle.
significance: Central narrative of Finland's national epic, directly inspiring Tolkien's Silmarillion and the concept of magical artifacts.

dna.moralLesson: Love is powerful, yet trust and restraint decide whether it heals or destroys.

name: Coyote Steals Fire
summary: In many Native American traditions, Coyote stole fire from the Fire Spirits to give to humanity. Through cunning and relay races with other animals, the fire was passed until it reached humanity. Coyote's cleverness is balanced by his foolishness. He is both creator and destroyer, teacher and troublemaker.
significance: Coyote is the most widespread trickster figure in Native American mythology, embodying paradox and creative disruption.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Native American ve Greek gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Tur farki: Trickster ve Quest odaklari ayridir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.

name: Cú Chulainn's Defense of Ulster
summary: When Queen Medb of Connacht invaded Ulster to steal the Brown Bull, the teenage hero Cú Chulainn single-handedly defended the province at a ford, fighting champions in single combat for months due to a curse on the Ulster warriors. His battle frenzy (ríastrad) transformed him into a terrifying creature.
significance: The central hero of the Ulster Cycle, embodying Celtic warrior ideals and the tragic price of supernatural gifts.

name: Amirani — Georgian Prometheus
summary: Amirani, son of a goddess, stole fire from the heavens and gave it to humanity. As punishment, he was chained to a rock in the Caucasus Mountains where an eagle eternally pecks at his heart. He still struggles to break free, causing earthquakes. The parallel with Prometheus is striking and ancient.
significance: A Caucasian fire-theft myth that may share a common origin with the Greek Prometheus story, predating Indo-European migration.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Georgian ve Greek gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Tur farki: Hero ve Quest odaklari ayridir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Georgian Mythology ve Greek Mythology arasindaki benzerlik, metin aktarimi ve temas aglariyla aciklanabilir; motifler yerel baglamda yeniden bicimlenmistir.

dna.moralLesson: Knowledge can elevate humanity, but it always carries ethical responsibility and cost.

name: Song of Kumarbi — Divine Succession
summary: Alalu was overthrown by Anu (heaven), who was overthrown by Kumarbi, who bit off and swallowed Anu's genitals. From this act, the storm god Teshub was born and eventually defeated Kumarbi. This divine succession myth closely parallels the Greek Theogony's account of Kronos and Zeus.
significance: Provides the direct Near Eastern source for Hesiod's Theogony, proving mythological transmission across cultures in the ancient world.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Hittite ve Greek gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Tur farki: Cosmology ve Creation odaklari ayridir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Hittite Mythology ile Greek Mythology arasindaki paralellik daha eski bir anlati havuzundan dallanma ihtimaline isaret eder; filolojik ve yapisal okumalar birlikte kullanilir.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Hittite ve Mesopotamian gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Tur farki: Cosmology ve Creation odaklari ayridir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Hittite Mythology ve Mesopotamian Mythology arasindaki benzerlik, metin aktarimi ve temas aglariyla aciklanabilir; motifler yerel baglamda yeniden bicimlenmistir.

dna.moralLesson: Order is never final; every generation must defend meaning against returning chaos.

name: Baal Cycle — Storm vs Sea vs Death
summary: Baal, storm god of the Canaanites, defeated Yamm (Sea) to establish order. He then confronted Mot (Death) and was killed, descending to the underworld. His sister-consort Anat defeated Mot, and Baal was resurrected. The cycle repeats with the seasons, ensuring agriculture and cosmic balance.
significance: The primary Canaanite mythological cycle, revealing deep parallels with both Mesopotamian and biblical narratives.

name: David of Sassoun
summary: The Armenian national epic tells of four generations of heroes from Sassoun. David, the greatest, wielded a magical sword and rode a supernatural horse. He defeated the tyrannical Msra Melik and liberated his people. His grandson Mher was trapped inside a rock for eternity, emerging only when the world becomes worthy.
significance: Armenia's national epic, preserved through oral tradition for a thousand years and recognized by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage.

name: Shango — Lord of Thunder
summary: Shango was a powerful king of Oyo who wielded thunder and fire. Betrayed by his subjects, he hanged himself but was deified as the orisha of thunder and justice. His three wives — Oya (wind), Oba (river), and Oshun (fertility) — became powerful orishas themselves. He is invoked for justice and strength.
significance: One of the most widely worshipped orishas worldwide, venerated in West Africa, Brazil, Cuba, Trinidad, and across the African diaspora.

name: The Blue Wolf and the Fallow Doe
summary: The Mongol people descended from Börte Chino (Blue Wolf) who mated with Gua Maral (Fallow Doe) after crossing the sea. Their offspring populated the steppe and eventually produced Genghis Khan, who united the Mongol tribes under Eternal Blue Heaven's mandate. The wolf remains a sacred ancestor symbol.
significance: Founding myth of the Mongol Empire, the largest contiguous land empire in history, establishing divine mandate for conquest.

name: Apedemak the Lion God
summary: Apedemak, the lion-headed warrior god of Kush, was worshipped as the supreme war deity. His temple at Naqa features him dispensing prisoners to the Meroitic king. The warrior queen Amanirenas invoked Apedemak when she led Kushite armies against Roman Egypt, famously losing an eye in battle but winning favorable terms.
significance: Represents indigenous Nubian religious traditions distinct from Egyptian influence, and the power of the Kandake (warrior queens) of Kush.

dna.moralLesson: Order is never final; every generation must defend meaning against returning chaos.

name: Jataka Tales — Buddha's Past Lives
summary: The Jataka tales recount over 500 previous lives of the Buddha as he accumulated merit toward enlightenment. In various incarnations as animals, kings, and ordinary people, the Bodhisattva demonstrated compassion, generosity, and wisdom. The stories teach moral lessons through allegory and adventure.
significance: The most important narrative tradition in Buddhism, spread across all of Asia and inspiring art, architecture, and moral education for 2,500 years.

dna.moralLesson: Knowledge can elevate humanity, but it always carries ethical responsibility and cost.

name: Etruscan Afterlife Banquet
summary: Etruscan tomb paintings depict joyful afterlife banquets where the deceased feast, dance, and enjoy music in the presence of guardian spirits. Vanth, a winged female figure, guided souls. Charun, with his hammer, guarded the underworld gate. The Etruscans viewed death as a transition to continued celebration.
significance: Etruscan afterlife beliefs directly influenced Roman funerary practices and reveal a unique Italian spiritual tradition prior to Greek influence.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Etruscan ve Egyptian gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Ayni turde olsalar da rituel islevleri ayrisir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Etruscan Mythology ve Egyptian Mythology arasindaki benzerlik, metin aktarimi ve temas aglariyla aciklanabilir; motifler yerel baglamda yeniden bicimlenmistir.

dna.moralLesson: Human flourishing requires aligning personal desire with communal and cosmic responsibility.

name: Quetzalcoatl's Exile
summary: Quetzalcoatl, the Feathered Serpent, ruled as a wise priest-king of Tula. His rival Tezcatlipoca tricked him into drunkenness and sin. Ashamed, Quetzalcoatl exiled himself, sailing east on a raft of serpents, vowing to return. This prophecy later played into the Spanish conquest when Cortés was initially mistaken for the returning god.
significance: One of the most complex Mesoamerican deities, whose departure myth had devastating historical consequences during the Spanish conquest.

name: Ahura Mazda vs Angra Mainyu
summary: Ahura Mazda (Wise Lord) created the world from pure thought. His adversary Angra Mainyu (Destructive Spirit) corrupted creation with disease, death, and evil. History is the 12,000-year cosmic battle between truth (asha) and falsehood (druj). At the end, a Saoshyant (savior) will purify the world in molten metal, defeating evil forever.
significance: The first systematic dualistic theology in history, directly influencing the concepts of Satan, heaven/hell, and final judgment in Abrahamic religions.

parallels.connectionExplanation: Persian / Zoroastrian Mythology ile Norse Mythology arasindaki baglanti kayda degerdir ancak literaturde nedensel model konusunda net uzlasi yoktur.

dna.moralLesson: Order is never final; every generation must defend meaning against returning chaos.

name: Deucalion's Flood
summary: Zeus sent a flood to destroy corrupt humanity. Deucalion and Pyrrha survived on a chest, landing on Mount Parnassus. They repopulated the earth by throwing stones over their shoulders — stones became people. This Greek flood narrative parallels the older Mesopotamian version closely.
significance: Greek version of the universal flood myth, linking Mediterranean and Near Eastern narrative traditions.

name: Theseus and the Minotaur
summary: Athens was forced to send seven youths and seven maidens to Crete to feed the Minotaur in the Labyrinth. Prince Theseus volunteered, aided by Ariadne's thread to navigate the maze. He slew the beast and freed Athens from the tribute. He abandoned Ariadne on Naxos.
significance: Classic labyrinth-quest myth that established Theseus as Athens' national hero.

name: Perseus and Medusa
summary: Perseus was sent to kill Medusa, the Gorgon whose gaze turned people to stone. Aided by Athena's mirror shield, Hermes' winged sandals, and Hades' cap of invisibility, he beheaded Medusa while looking at her reflection. He used her head to rescue Andromeda from a sea monster.
significance: Archetypal monster-slaying quest featuring divine aid and a petrifying foe.

name: Jason and the Golden Fleece
summary: Jason assembled the Argonauts to retrieve the Golden Fleece from Colchis. They faced clashing rocks, harpies, and fire-breathing bulls. Medea, the sorceress princess, helped Jason succeed out of love. Their return and tragic aftermath — Medea's revenge — remains one of mythology's darkest tales.
significance: The premier seafaring quest myth of the ancient world, showcasing heroic teamwork and tragic love.

name: Thor vs Jörmungandr
summary: Thor and the Midgard Serpent Jörmungandr are fated enemies. Thor once nearly caught the serpent while fishing with the giant Hymir, using an ox head as bait. At Ragnarök, they will fight to their mutual destruction — Thor slays the serpent but falls dead from its venom after nine steps.
significance: The quintessential Norse combat myth, embodying the warrior's acceptance of inevitable doom.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Norse ve Slavic gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.

parallels.connectionExplanation: Norse Mythology ile Slavic Mythology arasindaki paralellik daha eski bir anlati havuzundan dallanma ihtimaline isaret eder; filolojik ve yapisal okumalar birlikte kullanilir.

dna.moralLesson: Order is never final; every generation must defend meaning against returning chaos.

name: Manu and the Great Flood
summary: Manu, the first man, found a small fish that was Vishnu's avatar Matsya. The fish warned of a coming flood and instructed Manu to build a boat. When the flood came, Matsya grew enormous and towed the boat to safety on a mountain peak. Manu repopulated the earth through sacrifice and prayer.
significance: Hindu flood myth directly paralleling Mesopotamian and biblical accounts, demonstrating the universality of deluge narratives.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Hindu ve Mesopotamian gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Ayni turde olsalar da rituel islevleri ayrisir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Hindu Mythology ile Mesopotamian Mythology anlatilari benzer insanlik sorunlarina bagimsiz anlatilar gelistirmis olabilir; dogrudan temas zorunlu degildir.

name: Krishna's Divine Play (Lila)
summary: Born in a prison to defeat the tyrant Kamsa, Krishna was raised among cowherds. He performed miracles — lifting Mount Govardhana, dancing with the gopis, and playing enchanting flute. His love with Radha represents the soul's longing for the divine. He later served as Arjuna's charioteer in the Mahabharata.
significance: Krishna's narrative encompasses divine love, cosmic philosophy, and righteous action — central to Hindu devotional practice.

name: Pralaya — Cosmic Dissolution
summary: Hindu cosmology envisions vast cycles of creation and destruction. Each cosmic day of Brahma (kalpa) spans 4.32 billion years. At the end, Shiva dances the Tandava, dissolving the universe. Vishnu sleeps on the cosmic serpent Shesha in primordial waters. From his navel grows a lotus bearing Brahma, who creates anew.
significance: The most mathematically sophisticated cosmological myth in any tradition, with cycle lengths eerily close to modern scientific estimates of cosmic timeframes.

name: Chang'e Flies to the Moon
summary: The archer Hou Yi shot down nine of ten suns that were scorching the earth. He received the elixir of immortality but his wife Chang'e drank it and floated to the moon, where she lives forever with the Jade Rabbit. The Mid-Autumn Festival commemorates their eternal separation.
significance: Origin myth of the Mid-Autumn Festival, celebrated by billions, and inspiration for China's lunar exploration program (named Chang'e).

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Chinese ve Greek gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Ayni turde olsalar da rituel islevleri ayrisir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Chinese Mythology ile Greek Mythology arasindaki baglanti kayda degerdir ancak literaturde nedensel model konusunda net uzlasi yoktur.

dna.moralLesson: Knowledge can elevate humanity, but it always carries ethical responsibility and cost.

name: Four Dragon Kings of the Seas
summary: Four Dragon Kings rule the four seas surrounding China, controlling rain and weather. When they defied the Jade Emperor to bring rain to drought-stricken humans, they were transformed into four great rivers. The Dragon Kings' underwater crystal palaces are settings for many Chinese legends.
significance: Dragons in Chinese mythology are benevolent water deities, fundamentally different from Western dragon mythology.

dna.moralLesson: Human flourishing requires aligning personal desire with communal and cosmic responsibility.

name: Susanoo Slays Yamata no Orochi
summary: The storm god Susanoo, banished from heaven for his wild behavior, encountered an old couple weeping over their daughter Kushinadahime, the last of eight daughters devoured by an eight-headed serpent. Susanoo got the serpent drunk on sake, then slew it. From its tail he drew the sword Kusanagi, one of Japan's imperial regalia.
significance: The origin myth of the imperial sword Kusanagi, establishing Susanoo's complex role as both destructive and protective deity.

name: The Fox Wife (Kitsune)
summary: A beautiful woman married a man and bore his child. One night, startled by a dog, she revealed her true form — a fox spirit (kitsune). Though she loved her family, she was forced to leave, visiting only in dreams. Foxes with multiple tails possess greater power, with nine-tailed foxes being near-divine.
significance: The kitsune is one of Japan's most beloved yokai, representing the thin boundary between human and spirit worlds in Shinto belief.

dna.moralLesson: Knowledge can elevate humanity, but it always carries ethical responsibility and cost.

name: Gumiho — Nine-Tailed Fox
summary: The gumiho is a fox that has lived a thousand years, gaining the ability to transform into a beautiful woman. Unlike Japanese kitsune, Korean gumiho are typically malevolent, consuming the livers or hearts of men. Some stories tell of gumiho who genuinely fall in love and seek to become fully human through restraint.
significance: Korea's most famous supernatural creature, reflecting cultural attitudes about beauty, danger, and the possibility of redemption.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Korean ve Japanese gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Ayni turde olsalar da rituel islevleri ayrisir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Korean Mythology ve Japanese Mythology arasindaki benzerlik, metin aktarimi ve temas aglariyla aciklanabilir; motifler yerel baglamda yeniden bicimlenmistir.

dna.moralLesson: Knowledge can elevate humanity, but it always carries ethical responsibility and cost.

name: Maya Creation — Maize People
summary: The creator gods tried three times to make humans. Mud people dissolved, wood people were hollow and soulless. Finally, Xmucane ground white and yellow maize into dough, creating humans with blood and maize flesh. These humans were perfect — too perfect, so the gods clouded their vision to maintain divine authority.
significance: Creation narrative linking human existence to maize, the staff of life in Mesoamerican civilization.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Maya ve Chinese gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Ayni turde olsalar da rituel islevleri ayrisir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Maya Mythology ile Chinese Mythology arasindaki baglanti kayda degerdir ancak literaturde nedensel model konusunda net uzlasi yoktur.

name: Baba Yaga and Vasilisa
summary: Orphaned Vasilisa was sent by her stepmother to fetch fire from Baba Yaga, the fearsome witch who lives in a hut on chicken legs, surrounded by a fence of bones. Using her dead mother's magical doll for guidance, Vasilisa completed impossible tasks and obtained fire that burned her cruel stepfamily.
significance: One of Slavic folklore's most enduring tales, featuring a complex female antagonist who is both terrifying and necessary.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Slavic ve Native American gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Tur farki: Quest ve Trickster odaklari ayridir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Slavic Mythology ile Native American Mythology anlatilari benzer insanlik sorunlarina bagimsiz anlatilar gelistirmis olabilir; dogrudan temas zorunlu degildir.

dna.moralLesson: Knowledge can elevate humanity, but it always carries ethical responsibility and cost.

name: Book of Dede Korkut
summary: The epic tales of Dede Korkut recount the adventures of Oghuz Turkish heroes. Bamsi Beyrek endures trials to marry his beloved. Kan Turali fights monsters to win a warrior princess. The wise bard Dede Korkut advises and narrates, his songs shaping destiny. Each tale upholds honor, bravery, and loyalty.
significance: UNESCO-recognized masterpiece of Turkic oral literature, preserving nomadic warrior culture and pre-Islamic Central Asian traditions.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Turkic ve Celtic gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.

parallels.connectionExplanation: Turkish / Tengrist Mythology ile Celtic Mythology arasindaki baglanti kayda degerdir ancak literaturde nedensel model konusunda net uzlasi yoktur.

name: Anansi the Spider
summary: Anansi the Spider wanted to own all stories. The sky god Nyame set impossible prices: capture Onini the python, Osebo the leopard, Mmoboro the hornets, and Mmoatia the invisible fairy. Through cunning rather than strength, Anansi captured them all. Nyame made all stories 'spider stories' (Anansesem).
significance: One of Africa's most beloved trickster figures, carried to the Caribbean and Americas where Anansi stories became vehicles of resistance.

parallels.connectionExplanation: Yoruba Mythology ile Native American Mythology anlatilari benzer insanlik sorunlarina bagimsiz anlatilar gelistirmis olabilir; dogrudan temas zorunlu degildir.

name: Raven Steals the Light
summary: In the beginning, the world was dark. The Sky Chief kept the sun, moon, and stars in bentwood boxes. Raven transformed into a pine needle, was swallowed by the chief's daughter, and was reborn as her grandson. As a child, he opened the boxes one by one, releasing light into the world.
significance: Essential Northwest Coast creation myth, explaining how light came to the world through the trickster Raven's cleverness.

name: White Buffalo Calf Woman
summary: Two Lakota warriors encountered a beautiful woman in white. One approached with desire and was reduced to bones. The other was respectful. She brought the sacred pipe (chanunpa), teaching seven sacred rites including the Sun Dance, vision quest, and sweat lodge. She transformed into a white buffalo calf and vanished.
significance: Central to Lakota Sioux spirituality, establishing core ceremonies still practiced today. The birth of a white buffalo calf is considered a profound omen.

name: Väinämöinen's Creation Song
summary: The goddess Ilmatar lay floating on the primordial ocean. A teal laid seven eggs on her knee; they broke and formed the earth, sky, sun, and moon. From the waters Väinämöinen was born, an ancient sage who sang the world into being. His songs had the power to reshape reality itself.
significance: A creation through song — the idea that words and music have literal creative power is central to Finnish mythology.

name: Tlaloc and the Rain Sacrifice
summary: Tlaloc, the rain god, dwelt atop mountain peaks and in caves where clouds formed. He brought sustaining rain but also destructive storms, hail, and floods. Child sacrifices were offered to Tlaloc, their tears believed to bring rain. His paradise, Tlalocan, received those who died by water or lightning.
significance: Reveals the Aztec understanding that life-sustaining forces carried inherent danger, requiring continuous human reciprocity with nature.

dna.moralLesson: When moral order collapses, survival depends on humility, responsibility, and renewal.

name: Inti Raymi — Festival of the Sun
summary: Each winter solstice, the Inca held Inti Raymi, fearing the sun might not return. The Sapa Inca fasted, then led elaborate ceremonies with sacrifices, music, and feasting. Sacred flames were kindled with mirrors, and chicha (corn beer) was offered. The festival reinforced the Sapa Inca's divine solar lineage.
significance: The most important Inca festival, still celebrated today in Cusco by thousands, linking political power with solar cosmology.

name: Separation of Rangi and Papa
summary: Sky Father Rangi and Earth Mother Papa lay locked in eternal embrace, trapping their children in darkness. The children debated how to separate them. Tane Mahuta, god of forests, pushed them apart with his legs. Tawhirimatea, god of storms, was furious and attacked his brothers. Rangi's tears became rain.
significance: A creation-through-separation myth unique to Polynesia, explaining the origin of weather, seasons, and natural conflict.

name: Sedna — Mistress of the Sea
summary: Sedna was a beautiful Inuit woman tricked into marrying a bird spirit. Her father Anguta rescued her by kayak, but a storm threatened to capsize them. He threw Sedna overboard; when she clung to the boat, he cut off her fingers. Her fingers became seals, walruses, and whales. She sank to rule the sea floor.
significance: Central Inuit deity who controls marine animals essential for survival. Shamans must comb her tangled hair to release the animals for hunting.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Native American ve Chinese gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.

dna.moralLesson: Human flourishing requires aligning personal desire with communal and cosmic responsibility.

name: The Songlines — Walking the Dreaming
summary: During the Dreaming, Ancestor Beings walked across Australia singing the world into existence. Each feature — rock, waterhole, hill — was created by their songs. Aboriginal people maintain these songlines as navigational paths, spiritual practices, and legal codes. Walking a songline connects past creation with present reality.
significance: An integrated system of law, navigation, religion, ecology, and music unmatched in any other culture, spanning 60,000+ years.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Aboriginal ve Finnish gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Tur farki: Cosmology ve Creation odaklari ayridir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Aboriginal Australian Mythology ile Finnish / Kalevala Mythology anlatilari benzer insanlik sorunlarina bagimsiz anlatilar gelistirmis olabilir; dogrudan temas zorunlu degildir.

dna.moralLesson: Order is never final; every generation must defend meaning against returning chaos.

name: Journey to Mictlan
summary: After death, most Aztec souls traveled to Mictlan through nine challenging layers over four years. They crossed rivers of blood, passed between clashing mountains, endured razor-sharp winds, and finally stood before the death lord Mictlantecuhtli. A hairless dog (xoloitzcuintli) guided the soul through the underworld.
significance: Aztec afterlife was not reward or punishment but a difficult journey. The Day of the Dead (Día de los Muertos) partially derives from Mictlan beliefs.

name: Väinämöinen's Journey to Tuonela
summary: Väinämöinen journeyed to Tuonela, the Finnish underworld, seeking magical knowledge. He crossed the dark river and was received by the death goddess Tuonetar, who offered him beer of forgetfulness. Iron nets were cast to trap him. Using his shape-shifting powers, Väinämöinen escaped as a snake, warning others never to visit Tuonela voluntarily.
significance: Finnish underworld journey comparable to Odysseus and Orpheus descents, emphasizing the danger of seeking forbidden knowledge.

name: Purusha Sacrifice — Vedic Creation
summary: The cosmic being Purusha was sacrificed by the gods. From his body, the world was created: his mouth became brahmins, arms became warriors, thighs became merchants, feet became servants. From his mind came the moon, eyes the sun, breath the wind. This primordial sacrifice established cosmic and social order.
significance: One of Hinduism's oldest creation hymns, establishing the theological basis for the varna (caste) system and the concept of cosmic sacrifice.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Hindu ve Norse gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Ayni turde olsalar da rituel islevleri ayrisir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Hindu Mythology ile Norse Mythology anlatilari benzer insanlik sorunlarina bagimsiz anlatilar gelistirmis olabilir; dogrudan temas zorunlu degildir.

name: Creation by Eternal Blue Heaven
summary: Eternal Blue Heaven (Möngke Tengri) created the world from primordial waters. He sent a duck to dive for mud from the ocean floor; from this mud he shaped the earth. The devil figure Erlik created mountains and swamps as obstacles. Tengri breathed soul into humans, while Erlik gave them disease and death.
significance: Mongolian creation narrative showing the cosmic diver motif common across northern Eurasia and linking Tengrist belief with shamanistic tradition.

name: Rod Creates the Universe
summary: Rod, the supreme creator, broke the cosmic egg to create the universe. Light and darkness, earth and sky separated. He created Svarog the sky-smith who forged the sun. The Rozhanitsy (Rod's daughters) wove the fates of all living beings. Rod breathed life into everything and retired to the highest heaven.
significance: The primary Slavic creation myth, preserved through folk memory despite centuries of Christian suppression.

name: Tengri and the World Tree
summary: The Turkic cosmos is organized around a great World Tree connecting three realms: the upper sky-realm of Tengri, the middle world of humans, and the lower realm of Erlik. Shamans climb the tree in trance to communicate between worlds. Sixteen-layered heavens and seven-layered underworld contain various spirits.
significance: The Turkic cosmic geography parallels the Norse Yggdrasil and forms the basis of Central Asian shamanic practice still alive today.

Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Turkish / Tengrist Mythology ile Norse Mythology arasindaki baglanti kayda degerdir ancak literaturde nedensel model konusunda net uzlasi yoktur.

name: Phoenician Cosmogony
summary: From primordial dark wind and chaos, Mot (a cosmic egg of mud) cracked open. Sun, moon, and stars emerged. Animals and then humans appeared on the shores of Phoenicia. El, the father of gods, established divine order. The craftsman god Kothar-wa-Khasis fashioned divine tools and temples.
significance: Phoenician creation merging indigenous Semitic concepts with Egyptian and Mesopotamian influences, reflecting their role as cultural intermediaries.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Phoenician ve Mesopotamian gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Ayni turde olsalar da rituel islevleri ayrisir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Phoenician / Canaanite Mythology ve Mesopotamian Mythology arasindaki benzerlik, metin aktarimi ve temas aglariyla aciklanabilir; motifler yerel baglamda yeniden bicimlenmistir.

name: The Dragon Illuyanka
summary: The Storm God was defeated by the dragon Illuyanka, who stole his heart and eyes. The goddess Inaras seduced Illuyanka with a feast, getting him drunk so a mortal could bind him. In another version, the Storm God's son married Illuyanka's daughter and recovered the organs, allowing his father to triumph.
significance: Anatolian dragon-slaying myth showing the storm-dragon combat pattern found across Indo-European mythologies.

name: Jebel Barkal — Sacred Mountain of Creation
summary: The Nubians believed Jebel Barkal was the primordial mound of creation where the god Amun dwelt inside the mountain. A natural rock pinnacle resembled a uraeus (royal cobra), confirming divine presence. This sacred geography legitimized Kushite kings as true pharaohs, heirs to the original creation.
significance: Nubian reinterpretation of Egyptian creation theology, centering sacred geography in Sudan rather than Egypt proper.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Nubian ve Egyptian gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Ayni turde olsalar da rituel islevleri ayrisir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Nubian / Kushite Mythology ve Egyptian Mythology arasindaki benzerlik, metin aktarimi ve temas aglariyla aciklanabilir; motifler yerel baglamda yeniden bicimlenmistir.

name: Birth of Vahagn the Dragon-Slayer
summary: Vahagn was born from cosmic fire — heaven and earth labored, the sea turned red, and from a reed stalk fire emerged, forming a golden-haired youth with eyes like suns. He slew dragons (vishaps) and stole hay from the Milky Way (the 'Straw-Thief's Way' in Armenian). He was Armenia's war god.
significance: One of the oldest Armenian mythological narratives, preserved in a birth hymn by Moses of Chorene, showing Indo-European fire-hero patterns.

name: The Golden Fleece in Colchis
summary: In Georgian tradition, King Aeetes of Colchis guarded the Golden Fleece — the skin of a divine ram that had rescued children from sacrifice. The fleece hung in a sacred grove guarded by a dragon. When Jason came with the Argonauts, Aeetes' daughter Medea betrayed her father out of love. The story reflects Colchis's historical gold wealth.
significance: Georgia (ancient Colchis) was famed for gold-panning using sheepskins, possibly the real origin of the Golden Fleece legend.

name: Metamorphoses — Tales of Transformation
summary: Ovid's Metamorphoses weaves 250 transformation myths into a continuous narrative from creation to Julius Caesar's apotheosis. Narcissus becomes a flower, Daphne a laurel tree, Arachne a spider, and Icarus falls from the sky. Each transformation reveals the consequences of hubris, desire, or divine whim.
significance: The single most influential mythological text in Western art, providing source material for Renaissance painting, Shakespeare, and countless later works.

name: Roman Creation — Ages of Man
summary: The Roman creation myth describes four ages: the Golden Age under Saturn, when the earth yielded crops without labor; the Silver Age; the Bronze Age of warfare; and the Iron Age of suffering. Each age saw moral decline. Saturn's Golden Age became the model for the Saturnalia festival.
significance: Roman version of the declining-ages concept found across Indo-European mythologies, influencing Western concepts of a lost paradise.

name: The Quest for the Holy Grail
summary: King Arthur's knights of the Round Table embarked on the quest for the Holy Grail, the cup used by Christ at the Last Supper. Only the pure-hearted Galahad succeeded, while Lancelot was denied for his adultery with Guinevere. The quest reveals each knight's spiritual worth and the limits of martial valor.
significance: The Grail quest merged Celtic mythology with Christian symbolism, creating one of Western literature's most enduring narrative archetypes.

name: Oisín in Tír na nÓg
summary: The warrior Oisín fell in love with Niamh of the Golden Hair, who brought him to Tír na nÓg (Land of the Young). He lived there for what seemed three years but was actually 300. Returning to Ireland, he was forbidden to touch the ground. When he fell from his horse, he aged instantly into an old man.
significance: The quintessential Celtic fairy tale of time displacement, reflecting the dangerous allure of the Otherworld and the irreversibility of mortal things.

dna.moralLesson: Knowledge can elevate humanity, but it always carries ethical responsibility and cost.

name: Tale of Chunhyang
summary: Chunhyang, the daughter of a gisaeng (courtesan), secretly married the nobleman's son Mongryong. When Mongryong left for Seoul, the corrupt governor Byeon Hakdo tried to force Chunhyang to be his concubine. She refused and was tortured. Mongryong returned as a secret royal inspector and saved her. Their love transcended class.
significance: Korea's most famous love story, performed as pansori (narrative singing), representing resistance against corruption and class barriers.

dna.moralLesson: Knowledge can elevate humanity, but it always carries ethical responsibility and cost.

name: Tages Rises from the Furrow
summary: While plowing a field near Tarquinia, a farmer's plow uncovered a child with the wisdom of an elder. This was Tages, a divine being who taught the Etruscans the art of haruspicy (reading entrails), the interpretation of lightning, and the sacred laws (Etrusca disciplina). He then vanished.
significance: Origin myth of Etruscan divination practices that later became central to Roman state religion.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Etruscan ve Greek gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Tur farki: Creation ve Quest odaklari ayridir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Etruscan Mythology ve Greek Mythology arasindaki benzerlik, metin aktarimi ve temas aglariyla aciklanabilir; motifler yerel baglamda yeniden bicimlenmistir.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Etruscan ve Aztec gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Tur farki: Creation ve Trickster odaklari ayridir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Etruscan Mythology ile Aztec Mythology arasindaki baglanti kayda degerdir ancak literaturde nedensel model konusunda net uzlasi yoktur.

dna.moralLesson: Knowledge can elevate humanity, but it always carries ethical responsibility and cost.

name: Pandora's Box
summary: Zeus created Pandora, the first woman, as punishment for Prometheus's theft of fire. Each god gave her gifts — beauty, cunning, curiosity. She was given a jar (pithos) and told never to open it. Curiosity overwhelmed her, releasing all evils into the world. Only Hope remained inside.
significance: Foundation myth explaining the origin of evil and suffering, and humanity's enduring capacity for hope.

dna.moralLesson: Knowledge can elevate humanity, but it always carries ethical responsibility and cost.

name: Echo and Narcissus
summary: The beautiful Narcissus rejected all lovers, including the nymph Echo who faded to only a voice. Nemesis cursed him to fall in love with his own reflection. Unable to look away from the pool, Narcissus wasted away and was transformed into the flower bearing his name.
significance: Origin of the term narcissism and a profound meditation on self-love, vanity, and the destructive nature of beauty.

name: The Trojan Horse
summary: After ten years besieging Troy, the Greeks built a hollow wooden horse and hid warriors inside. They feigned retreat. Despite Laocoön's warning, the Trojans brought the horse inside their walls. At night, Greek soldiers emerged and opened the gates. Troy burned in a single devastating night.
significance: History's most famous military stratagem, giving rise to the Trojan Horse metaphor for deceptive infiltration.

name: Theft of the Mead of Poetry
summary: The Mead of Poetry was brewed from the blood of the wisest being, Kvasir. Odin infiltrated the giant Suttung's mountain by seducing his daughter Gunnlöð. He drank all three cauldrons of mead and escaped as an eagle, spitting the mead into vessels in Asgard. Some spilled to earth, giving mortals poetry.
significance: Explains the origin of poetic inspiration and Odin's role as patron of poets and wisdom-seekers.

parallels.connectionExplanation: Norse Mythology ve Finnish / Kalevala Mythology arasindaki benzerlik, metin aktarimi ve temas aglariyla aciklanabilir; motifler yerel baglamda yeniden bicimlenmistir.

name: Narasimha — The Man-Lion Avatar
summary: The demon king Hiranyakashipu received a boon: he could not be killed by man or animal, inside or outside, by day or night. He terrorized his devoted son Prahlada who worshipped Vishnu. Vishnu appeared as Narasimha (half-man, half-lion) at twilight, on a threshold, and killed the demon on his lap.
significance: A masterful theological narrative demonstrating that divine power transcends all logical constraints and loopholes.

name: Fu Xi and the Eight Trigrams
summary: The sage-emperor Fu Xi observed patterns in nature — the markings on a dragon-horse, turtle shells, and the stars. He devised the eight trigrams (bagua), capturing the fundamental principles of reality: heaven, earth, fire, water, mountain, lake, wind, and thunder. These became the basis of the I Ching.
significance: Foundation myth of Chinese philosophy, mathematics, and divination that influenced all of East Asian civilization.

name: Yu the Great Controls the Flood
summary: Great floods threatened China. Yu's father Gun tried to stop them by stealing magic soil from heaven. He failed. Yu spent thirteen years channeling the waters through drainage, never visiting home even when passing by. He divided the land into nine provinces and became the first emperor of the Xia dynasty.
significance: China's foundational flood myth, establishing the ideal of selfless service and hard work that defined Chinese imperial virtue.

name: Tanabata — The Star-Crossed Lovers
summary: Orihime (Vega) wove beautiful cloth for her father the Sky King. She fell in love with the cowherd Hikoboshi (Altair). They neglected their work, so the Sky King separated them on opposite sides of the Milky Way. They may meet only once a year on the seventh of July, when magpies form a bridge.
significance: Origin of the Tanabata festival, celebrated across Japan and East Asia, based on the Chinese Qixi legend.

name: Urashima Tarō — The Fisherman's Journey
summary: Fisherman Urashima Tarō rescued a turtle, which took him to the Dragon Palace under the sea. He married the princess Otohime and lived happily for three days. Returning home, he found 300 years had passed. He opened a forbidden box she gave him and aged instantly to dust.
significance: Japanese parallel to Rip Van Winkle and Celtic Tír na nÓg — time displacement tales warning about the boundary between human and spirit worlds.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Japanese ve Celtic gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Tur farki: Quest ve Love odaklari ayridir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Japanese Mythology ile Celtic Mythology anlatilari benzer insanlik sorunlarina bagimsiz anlatilar gelistirmis olabilir; dogrudan temas zorunlu degildir.

dna.moralLesson: Knowledge can elevate humanity, but it always carries ethical responsibility and cost.

name: The Flood of the Wood People
summary: In the second creation, the gods made humans from wood. These people could speak but lacked hearts and minds, showing no gratitude to their creators. The gods sent a great flood of black rain and resin. Animals and even their own tools attacked the wood people. Their descendants became monkeys.
significance: Maya version of the universal flood narrative, uniquely explaining the origin of monkeys and emphasizing the importance of gratitude and consciousness.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Maya ve Mesopotamian gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Ayni turde olsalar da rituel islevleri ayrisir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Maya Mythology ile Mesopotamian Mythology arasindaki baglanti kayda degerdir ancak literaturde nedensel model konusunda net uzlasi yoktur.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Maya ve Aztec gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Tur farki: Cosmology ve Creation odaklari ayridir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Maya Mythology ve Aztec Mythology arasindaki benzerlik, metin aktarimi ve temas aglariyla aciklanabilir; motifler yerel baglamda yeniden bicimlenmistir.

dna.moralLesson: When moral order collapses, survival depends on humility, responsibility, and renewal.

name: The Rusalki — Water Spirits
summary: Rusalki are water spirits — souls of young women who died violently near water. They emerge during Rusalka Week in early summer, dancing in moonlit meadows and forests. Their beauty enchants young men, whom they lure into rivers to drown. Green wreaths and garlic protect against them.
significance: The rusalki tradition reveals pre-Christian Slavic beliefs about unquiet dead, water spirits, and feminine power, preserved in folk practice across Eastern Europe.

name: Alp Er Tunga — The Great King
summary: Alp Er Tunga (identified with the Persian Afrasiyab) was a legendary Turkic king who waged wars against Iran. His death was sung in elegies across the Turkic world. Mahmud of Kashgar recorded mourning poems in the Divan. He represented the ideal Turkic ruler — brave, just, and fierce in battle.
significance: One of the earliest named Turkic heroes, bridging Turkic and Persian literary traditions and establishing the warrior-king archetype.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Turkic ve Greek gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Tur farki: Hero ve War odaklari ayridir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Turkish / Tengrist Mythology ile Greek Mythology arasindaki baglanti kayda degerdir ancak literaturde nedensel model konusunda net uzlasi yoktur.

name: Zal and the Simorgh
summary: Zal, born with white hair, was abandoned on Mount Damavand by his ashamed father Sam. The Simorgh, a benevolent mythical bird, raised him. When Sam repented, the Simorgh returned Zal with one of her feathers — when burned, she would come to his aid. Zal married Rudabeh and fathered the hero Rostam.
significance: The Simorgh represents divine wisdom and nurturing in Persian mythology, and Zal's story explores rejection, adoption, and the healing of family bonds.

name: Buddha's Enlightenment — Temptation by Mara
summary: Under the Bodhi tree, Siddhartha meditated for 49 days seeking enlightenment. Mara, lord of illusion, attacked him with armies, tempted him with beautiful daughters, and challenged his right to awaken. Siddhartha touched the earth, calling it as witness. Mara fled, and Siddhartha became the Buddha — the Awakened One.
significance: The pivotal moment of Buddhism — the defeat of illusion through mindfulness, widely depicted across all Buddhist cultures.

dna.moralLesson: Human flourishing requires aligning personal desire with communal and cosmic responsibility.

name: Pele — Goddess of Volcanoes
summary: Pele traveled across the Pacific creating volcanic islands until she settled in Hawaii's Kīlauea. She is both creator and destroyer — lava from her anger forms new land. Her rivalry with the pig god Kamapua'a and her love for the mortal Lohiau drive dramatic narratives. She is a living deity still honored today.
significance: Pele represents one of the few mythological deities whose domain — active volcanism — is visually verifiable and ongoing.

name: How Fire Was Stolen (Aboriginal)
summary: In various Aboriginal traditions, fire was guarded by selfish keepers. Crow (or other clever animals) devised schemes to steal it for the people. In one version, Crow tricked the fire-keepers into opening their sacred box, grabbed a burning stick, and flew away, scorching his feathers permanently black.
significance: Aboriginal fire-theft myth paralleling global Promethean traditions but with uniquely Australian characters and ecological context.

name: Ifa Divination — Orunmila's Gift
summary: Orunmila, the orisha of wisdom, witnessed creation and knows the destiny of all beings. He gave humanity the Ifa divination system — 256 odu (signs) containing stories, medicines, and wisdom for every life situation. A babalawo (priest) casts palm nuts or chains to read destiny. Eshu carries messages between humans and orishas.
significance: Ifa divination is a UNESCO-recognized Intangible Cultural Heritage, a living philosophical and spiritual system practiced by millions worldwide.

name: The Shaman's Journey to the Sky
summary: Mongolian shamans enter ecstatic trance, their soul traveling up the World Tree or riding spirit horses to reach the sky realms. They pass through nine or thirteen heavens to petition Tengri for healing, rain, or guidance. The shaman's drum is their spirit horse, and their costume represents the cosmos.
significance: Mongolian shamanism preserves one of the oldest forms of spiritual practice, with roots possibly reaching back to the Upper Paleolithic.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Mongolian ve Finnish gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Tur farki: Cosmology ve Afterlife odaklari ayridir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Mongolian Mythology ile Finnish / Kalevala Mythology arasindaki baglanti kayda degerdir ancak literaturde nedensel model konusunda net uzlasi yoktur.

name: The Warrior Queens (Kandakes)
summary: The Kandakes (warrior queens) of Kush were both political rulers and living goddesses. Amanirenas led armies against Augustus's Rome, blinding herself in battle. Amanishakheto accumulated enormous treasure. They ruled with divine authority from Apedemak, building pyramids and temples that rivaled Egypt's achievements.
significance: Nubian warrior queens challenge modern stereotypes about women's roles in ancient civilizations and the limitations of African political power.

dna.moralLesson: Human flourishing requires aligning personal desire with communal and cosmic responsibility.

name: Pachamama — Earth Mother
summary: Pachamama is the living earth, a nurturing goddess who provides food, water, and shelter. In return, she demands respect and offerings (despachos). She can cause earthquakes when angry. During planting and harvest, chicha and coca leaves are offered. She is not merely a nature goddess — she IS the earth, alive and conscious.
significance: Pachamama worship survived Spanish colonization and is now constitutionally recognized in Bolivia and Ecuador, representing one of the most resilient indigenous spiritual traditions.

dna.moralLesson: Human flourishing requires aligning personal desire with communal and cosmic responsibility.

name: The Descent to Xibalba
summary: Hun Hunahpu and his twin descended to Xibalba, the underworld, summoned by the Lords of Death who were angered by their ball-playing. They failed the tests — the Dark House, Cold House, Jaguar House, Fire House, and Bat House. They were sacrificed, and Hun Hunahpu's head was placed in a calabash tree.
significance: The underworld trials of the father generation set up the Hero Twins' later revenge, forming a two-generational narrative rare in world mythology.

name: Yima's Vara — Persian Flood Myth
summary: Ahura Mazda warned King Yima of a coming winter that would destroy all life. He instructed Yima to build a vara (enclosure) and fill it with the finest specimens of every living thing — seeds, animals, and humans. After the great winter passed, Yima's vara repopulated the world.
significance: An Iranian flood/preservation myth independent of Mesopotamian tradition, establishing an ark narrative focused on cosmic winter rather than water.

parallels.connectionExplanation: Persian / Zoroastrian Mythology ve Mesopotamian Mythology arasindaki benzerlik, metin aktarimi ve temas aglariyla aciklanabilir; motifler yerel baglamda yeniden bicimlenmistir.

name: Navajo Emergence — Four Worlds
summary: The Navajo people emerged through four colored worlds — Black, Blue, Yellow, and White. In each world, conflicts caused by Coyote forced migration upward. Spider Woman taught weaving; First Man and First Woman brought sacred medicine bundles. Through a reed, the people climbed into the Fifth World — the present glittering world.
significance: The Navajo emergence myth grounds their entire legal, medical, and ceremonial system in a narrative of upward progress through different realms.

name: Zhurong vs Gonggong — Battle of Fire and Water
summary: The fire god Zhurong battled the water god Gonggong for supremacy. Defeated, Gonggong smashed his head against Mount Buzhou, one of the pillars holding up the sky. The sky tilted, causing floods and fires. Nüwa repaired the sky with five-colored stones and cut off a turtle's legs as new pillars.
significance: Explains why rivers in China flow east, why the sky tilts northwest, and provides the cosmic context for Nüwa's sky-repair myth.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Chinese ve Slavic gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.

Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Chinese Mythology ile Slavic Mythology arasindaki baglanti kayda degerdir ancak literaturde nedensel model konusunda net uzlasi yoktur.

name: Princess Pyeonggang and the Fool Ondal
summary: The spirited princess cried so much that her father promised her to the village fool Ondal. She left the palace and married him, training him in martial arts and scholarship. Ondal became the nation's greatest general, proving that talent and love transcend social status. He died in battle defending the kingdom.
significance: A beloved Korean folktale celebrating social mobility, the transformative power of love, and the idea that potential exists in everyone.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Korean ve Korean gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.

dna.moralLesson: Love is powerful, yet trust and restraint decide whether it heals or destroys.

name: The Birth of Ganesha
summary: Parvati created a boy from turmeric paste to guard her bath. When Shiva returned and the boy blocked him, Shiva beheaded him in rage. Parvati's grief was so great that Shiva promised to restore the child with the head of the first creature found — an elephant. Thus Ganesha was born, remover of obstacles and lord of beginnings.
significance: Ganesha is one of the most worshipped deities worldwide, invoked at the start of every new venture, journey, and ceremony in Hindu practice.

name: The Morrígan — Phantom Queen of Battle
summary: The Morrígan is a triple goddess of war, fate, and death. She appears as a crow over battlefields, selecting who will die. She offered Cú Chulainn her love, and when refused, became his enemy — yet also his protector. Before battles, she washed the armor of those fated to die at the ford.
significance: The Morrígan represents the Celtic concept of sovereignty as feminine and the intimate connection between love, war, and death.

dna.moralLesson: Love is powerful, yet trust and restraint decide whether it heals or destroys.

name: Huitzilopochtli vs Coyolxauhqui
summary: Coatlicue became pregnant from a ball of feathers. Her daughter Coyolxauhqui and 400 brothers plotted to kill her in shame. At the moment of attack, Huitzilopochtli was born fully armed, dismembering Coyolxauhqui and hurling her down Mount Coatepec. This battle is reenacted daily as the sun defeats the moon and stars.
significance: Central myth justifying Aztec warfare and human sacrifice — the sun god needed blood to win his daily battle against darkness.

dna.moralLesson: When moral order collapses, survival depends on humility, responsibility, and renewal.

name: Proserpina and the Pomegranate
summary: Pluto abducted Proserpina to the underworld. Her mother Ceres caused all plants to die. Jupiter brokered a deal but Proserpina had eaten pomegranate seeds — binding her to six months below. Her annual return brings spring; her departure brings winter. The Eleusinian-style mysteries spread this cult across the Roman Empire.
significance: Roman adaptation of the Persephone myth that became one of the empire's most popular religious narratives.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Roman ve Greek gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.
Ayni turde olsalar da rituel islevleri ayrisir.
Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Roman Mythology ile Greek Mythology arasindaki paralellik daha eski bir anlati havuzundan dallanma ihtimaline isaret eder; filolojik ve yapisal okumalar birlikte kullanilir.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Roman ve Mesopotamian gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.

Mekansal ve tarihsel baglam sembolik islevleri degistirir.
parallels.connectionExplanation: Roman Mythology ve Mesopotamian Mythology arasindaki benzerlik, metin aktarimi ve temas aglariyla aciklanabilir; motifler yerel baglamda yeniden bicimlenmistir.

dna.moralLesson: Human flourishing requires aligning personal desire with communal and cosmic responsibility.

name: Lemminkäinen's Death and Resurrection
summary: The reckless hero Lemminkäinen was killed trying to shoot the swan of Tuonela. His body was hacked to pieces and thrown into the river of the dead. His mother, sensing his death, raked the river with a copper rake, gathered every fragment, and sang him back to life — the power of a mother's love and magic defeating death.
significance: A uniquely feminine resurrection narrative where maternal love and song-magic overcome death, contrasting with typical male-driven hero resurrection myths.

name: Daedalus and Icarus
summary: The master craftsman Daedalus built the Labyrinth for King Minos, then was imprisoned with his son Icarus. He crafted wings from feathers and wax. He warned Icarus not to fly too high or too low. Icarus, exhilarated, soared toward the sun. The wax melted and he fell into the sea.
significance: Archetypal cautionary tale about hubris, ambition, and the danger of ignoring wise counsel.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Greek ve Greek gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.

name: Freyja and the Brísingamen
summary: Freyja desired the Brísingamen, a necklace of incomparable beauty forged by four dwarves. She spent a night with each dwarf to obtain it. Loki stole it on Odin's orders, transforming into a flea to unpin the clasp. Heimdall fought Loki to recover it. The necklace became Freyja's most treasured possession.
significance: Reveals the complex Norse view of desire, beauty, and divine femininity — Freyja is both shamelessly desirous and utterly powerful.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Norse ve Greek gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.

parallels.connectionExplanation: Norse Mythology ile Greek Mythology arasindaki baglanti kayda degerdir ancak literaturde nedensel model konusunda net uzlasi yoktur.

dna.moralLesson: Cunning can challenge power, but deceit always leaves moral consequences.

name: The Destruction of Mankind (Sekhmet)
summary: Ra sent his eye (Hathor/Sekhmet) to punish disobedient humanity. The lioness goddess Sekhmet went on a blood-fueled rampage, threatening to destroy all humans. To stop her, the gods dyed beer red with ochre to resemble blood. Sekhmet drank it, became drunk, and fell asleep, transforming back into gentle Hathor.
significance: Explores the dual nature of divine feminine power — nurturing Hathor and destructive Sekhmet are the same goddess.

parallels.connectionExplanation: Egyptian Mythology ile Hindu Mythology arasindaki baglanti kayda degerdir ancak literaturde nedensel model konusunda net uzlasi yoktur.

name: Shiva's Cosmic Dance (Nataraja)
summary: Shiva performs the Tandava, the cosmic dance that creates, sustains, and destroys the universe. As Nataraja (Lord of the Dance), he dances within a ring of fire. One foot crushes the dwarf Apasmara (ignorance), while the other is raised in liberation. His drum sounds creation, his fire hand destruction.
significance: One of the world's most recognizable religious icons, the Nataraja represents the dynamic nature of the universe — destruction and creation as one.

name: Legend of the White Snake
summary: A white snake spirit transformed into a beautiful woman and fell in love with the mortal Xu Xian. They married and she used her powers to help the sick. The monk Fahai exposed her true form and imprisoned her under Leifeng Pagoda. Green Snake eventually freed her. Their love transcended the boundary between human and spirit.
significance: One of China's four great folktales, exploring the tension between genuine love and Confucian/Buddhist moral order.

divergences: Teolojik baglam farki: Chinese ve Japanese gelenekleri farkli ilahi hiyerarsiler kurar.

dna.moralLesson: Love is powerful, yet trust and restraint decide whether it heals or destroys.
